## Summary

4-Bromoacetanilide from acetanilide. This is sample data; the quantities are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acetanilide | 103-84-4 | 135.17 | 1.352 g | 10.0 | 1.0 |
| Sodium bromide | 7647-15-6 | 102.89 | 1.235 g | 12.0 | 1.2 |
| Sodium hypochlorite | 7681-52-9 | 74.44 | 1 M aqueous solution, 12 mL | 12.0 | 1.2 |
| Acetic acid | 64-19-7 | 60.05 | 10 mL | – | – |
| Ethanol | 64-17-5 | 46.07 | 10 mL | – | – |
| Sodium hydrogen sulfite | 7631-90-5 | 104.06 | aqueous solution, as needed | – | – |

## Procedure

1. Dissolve acetanilide in ethanol and acetic acid.
2. Add sodium bromide with stirring.
3. Cool the flask in a water bath.
4. Add aqueous sodium hypochlorite gradually.
5. Stir for 30 minutes at room temperature.
6. Add aqueous sodium hydrogen sulfite to destroy residual oxidant.
7. Add water and cool in ice.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the precipitate by suction filtration, wash with water and dry.

## Characterization

White solid; literature melting point approximately 165–168 °C. IR (ATR): amide C=O near 1660 cm⁻¹; ¹H NMR: two aromatic doublets near δ 7.4–7.6.

## Notes

1. Add hypochlorite slowly in a fume hood: bromine is generated in situ from bromide and hypochlorite; acidified hypochlorite can release chlorine.
2. Check the identity and purity of the product before further use.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Bromine is generated during addition; it is toxic and corrosive. Acetanilide: harmful if swallowed; Sodium bromide: may irritate eyes; Sodium hypochlorite: corrosive; releases toxic chlorine with acid; Acetic acid: corrosive; flammable when concentrated; Ethanol: highly flammable; Sodium hydrogen sulfite: harmful if swallowed; releases irritating sulfur dioxide with acid; 4-Bromoacetanilide: dust or vapour may irritate. Work in a fume hood with gloves and eye protection. Collect aqueous and organic waste separately according to local rules.
